add_ons.description: All three Flipper One modules in one add-on

story_text:
Flipper One is a portable, standalone Linux computer that you can use as a platform for building your own projects. Turn it into a Network Multi-tool, Radio Lab, Home IoT Server, or Desktop Computer. Expand its capabilities with high-speed M.2 modules and GPIO accessories. Connect 5G modems, SDR radios, SSD storage, LoRa modules, and more.
Flipper One runs on completely open-source Linux firmware with a mainline kernel. This means full compatibility with the latest kernel versions:
- Mainline Linux kernel support — full support in upstream Linux kernel.
- No binary blobs — no proprietary code or binaries in the boot process.
- No vendor-locked BSP — free from outdated vendor board support packages.
Our goal is to create a fully upstream-supported ARM computer that never becomes outdated, along with a well-documented platform giving the community maximum freedom to customize. To pull this off, we've partnered with the Collabora team, well-known contributors to the Linux kernel.
Flipper Zero and Flipper One are completely different projects built for different tasks. The easiest way to think about it is in terms of networking layers:
- Layer 0 (Zero) — Offline point-to-point access-control protocols: NFC, low-frequency RFID, Sub-1 GHz radio, Infrared, wired protocols like iButton, UART, SPI, I2C. Based on a low-power microcontroller.
- Layer 1 (One) — Everything that's IP-connected: Wi-Fi, Ethernet, 5G, and satellite. It's all about networking, data transfer, and high-performance computing. An open Linux toolkit running on powerful hardware, enough computing power to handle SDR and local AI.
So they're not "newer" and "older" generations of the same product. Flipper One doesn't replace Flipper Zero — they're different categories of devices. Comparing them directly would be like comparing a hammer to a screwdriver.
Two independent processors work in parallel controlling different subsystems in Flipper One. This architecture lets you control the device from the built-in LCD, even when Linux is powered off or rebooting, so you never lose access to the user interface.
## Why 2 processors?
- Low-power MCU (Raspberry Pi RP2350) — manages LCD display, buttons, power and controls system boot stages.
- High-performance CPU (Rockchip RK3576) — runs Linux kernel and user apps, and manages high-speed peripheral interfaces: Ethernet, Wi-Fi, PCIe, USB, HDMI, etc.
The idea behind the 2-processor architecture is to make Flipper One a fully standalone device that remains operational even if the user completely breaks the Linux system. It allows to recover OS without needing an external computer or additional software.
Most single-board computers require several cables to operate: one for power, another for UART console, and so on. We decided to fix that. With Flipper One, a single USB-C cable is enough for most tasks.
## Pocket Linux Lab via USB-C
Connect Flipper One to a laptop with a single USB-C cable to get SSH console access and charge the device at the same time. No extra adapters are needed for Linux console access or power — Flipper One can simultaneously emulate a USB network adapter, a serial (COM port), or disk device.
- Power IN/OUT — the USB-C1 port supports 5–20 V Power Delivery and can charge Flipper One or power your laptop.
- Device Emulation — the same port also emulates a USB network adapter, serial device, or disk drive. All at speeds of up to 5 Gbps.
Desktop Mode via USB-C
Connect Flipper One to an external display using a single USB Type-C cable and get a full desktop experience.
- USB DisplayPort Alt Mode — video output at 4K@120Hz to an external display over a single USB-C cable.
- USB Host + Charging — connect peripherals such as a keyboard and mouse through your monitor’s USB hub while charging Flipper One over the same cable.
## Recovery & Debugger via USB-C
We wanted to make alternative firmware development for Flipper One easier. You can debug and perform a full system recovery through the same primary USB-C port (USB-C1). For most development tasks, you won't need a separate debugger.
Using the USB-C1 port, you can access the debug console & BOOTSEL mode for recovering the RP2350 MCU, and MaskROM mode for recovering the RK3576 CPU.
Multi-WAN Network Router — connect up to 5 uplinks simultaneously. Configure dynamic routing, failover, load balancing, and firewall rules. Use it simultaneously as a Wi‑Fi hotspot and client. Tunnel traffic through a VPN and multiple gateways.
- 2× Gigabit Ethernet — two independent WAN/LAN ports, each running at 1 Gbps. Can be used for a transparent bridge, MitM sniffing, and more.
- Wi-Fi 6E — based on the MT7921AUN chipset with monitor mode support. Covers 2.4/5/6 GHz bands and can run as both a Wi-Fi Client (STA) and a Hotspot (AP).
- Cellular modem — 5G or LTE modem via the M.2 expansion module, with support for external antennas. Accepts a physical Nano SIM (4FF) and eSIM.
- USB Ethernet — up to 5 Gbps emulated over USB-C. Connect your laptop or smartphone via a USB cable to add an extra network interface. Works via USB CDC-NCM, so no drivers are required.
Out of the box, Flipper One can work as a gateway to any network, a multi-hotspot bridge, an inline Ethernet sniffer, a USB Wi-Fi/Ethernet adapter for a PC or phone.
Network Scanner
Analyze wired and wireless IP networks: discover active hosts, scan for open ports and services, detect network attacks and report anomalies. Flipper One comes with built-in apps for network analysis, mapping network topology, and detecting host misconfigurations.It can also identify vulnerable and outdated services, act as a honeypot to detect network scanning activity, and save the results as exportable reports.
We want to build the most versatile integrated Wi-Fi into Flipper One — it needs to support all the features required for Wi-Fi network analysis, including monitor mode and packet injection, as well as all common Wi-Fi frequency bands.
For now, we've settled on the popular MediaTek MT7921U chipset. It's modern enough to support all three Wi-Fi frequency bands and checks almost every box on our list. It also supports Bluetooth and Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE).
The chipset has even more potential, as it allows to capture raw I/Q samples 💀. Join us in exploring its capabilities >>
To make Flipper One work as a portable hotspot worldwide, we're developing an official 5G Cellular Module based on the Quectel RM520 modem, which supports a wide range of global cellular bands and delivers download speeds of up to 1 Gbps! It can use either Flipper One's built-in eSIM or a physical SIM card.
We want to give networking geeks the ultimate travel router, with their custom VPNs, proxies, routing rules, NAS, and firewalls. A hotspot you can take anywhere, with your entire network setup, without having to swap SIM cards in your phone.
The 5G Cellular Module connects to the M.2 expansion slot and replaces the original Flipper One's back plate. The module consists of three main parts: an M.2 modem card, a metal back plate with integrated SMA female antenna connectors, and four compact antennas. The modem is enclosed in a metal housing that doubles as a heatsink and forms the new back of the device.
## Connect your directional 5G antenna
We designed the 5G module with full-size SMA female connectors, allowing you to attach external antennas of your choice. This is especially useful in areas with poor cellular coverage, where a directional antenna may be the only way to get a reliable signal.
[画像: At this photo Flipper One is connected to a professional-grade Waveform QuadPro 4×4 MIMO directional 5G antenna. This allowed us to get a stable internet connection in a remote area with bad cellular coverage.]
In this photo Flipper One is connected to a professional-grade Waveform QuadPro 4×4 MIMO directional 5G antenna. This allowed us to get a stable internet connection in a remote area with bad cellular coverage.
We've faced this problem ourselves: there are almost no compact 5G hotspots on the market that let you connect a proper 4×4 MIMO directional antenna. Your options are either outdated USB dongles with tiny TS9 connectors or bulky industrial routers.
The idea behind the Flipper One 5G Cellular Module is to pack a professional, high-speed 5G modem into the smallest possible form factor, while still allowing you to connect full-size, professional-grade external antennas.
Flipper One has a built-in eSIM chip that comes pre‑provisioned with a Flipper SIM data plan. The eSIM contacts are routed to the M.2 port, allowing the built-in eSIM to work with any M.2 modem installed in Flipper One — including the official Flipper 5G Cellular module.
## Flipper SIM FAQ
> What is Flipper SIM?
Flipper SIM is our outage-proof SIM card project for network geeks. We want to build features we ourselves miss from traditional mobile operators. The project is still in development, and we'll share more details later.
> Do I have to use Flipper eSIM with the 5G modem?
No. You can use your own physical SIM card instead and completely disable the built-in Flipper eSIM.
The core idea of Flipper One is an expandable hardware platform. Create your own specialized tool with a high-speed M.2 expansion module that installs inside the device, under the back plate.
M.2 port supports many types of modules — cellular or satellite modems, SDR modules, AI accelerators, SSDs (NVMe or SATA), and Wi-Fi cards via adapters.
## M.2 Port tech specs
The M.2 (NGFF) standard comes in many configurations and can support different interfaces within the same physical connector. We tried to pack as many interfaces as possible into Flipper One's M.2 slot: PCI Express, USB, SATA, and SIM card, along with additional interfaces not typically found in M.2, such as Serial Audio, UART, and I2C.
## Open Mounting system
We designed our own module mounting system to keep expansion modules securely in place, without leaving them loose or sticking out. To help the community create custom modules, we've made all the 3D models and technical drawings publicly available. This means anyone can design and 3D print their own custom module mounts.
🎥 In this video, our industrial designer Roman Galeev explains the mechanical design of Flipper One and its module mounting system.
DIY modules can be connected via the GPIO connector using standard 2.54 mm pin headers. To make the assembled device easier to carry around, the GPIO module is positioned along the device body and can be covered with a protective cover.
GPIO modules also have their own mounting system:
- Threaded inserts — the back plate and antenna rail have threads spaced in a grid with 2.54mm pitch, matching standard perfboard hole spacing. So you can just cut a piece of perfboard to size, solder your module onto it, and screw it to the Flipper One's back.
- Snap-fit notches — both sides of the body have notches for a snap-fit protective cover that adds rigidity to the whole assembly.
The GPIO port provides 3.3V and 5V power, connects to pins on both the MCU and CPU, and includes a USB 2.0 interface. The complete schematics and GPIO pinout are available here >>
The LoRa module comes ready to use with off-grid mesh communication protocols such as MeshCore, Meshtastic, and Reticulum. It can also work as a Walkie-Talkie, letting you communicate directly with other Flipper One devices.
These protocols will let users build P2P networks right out of the box, using existing community-driven infrastructure like MeshCore. Flipper One can also serve as a backup communication channel for IoT gateways.

risks: The biggest risk is the ongoing component shortage, particularly the disruption in the RAM market, where memory prices have increased many times over. If the crisis continues, it could cause significant delays to production and delivery. Our current production plans assume that memory prices will gradually come down. However, we cannot rule out adjusting some product specifications, including reducing the amount of RAM.

faq.q: Is Flipper One an upgrade to Flipper Zero?
faq.a: No. They are different devices built for different tasks. Flipper Zero works with offline access-control protocols: NFC, low-frequency RFID, Sub-1 GHz radio, and infrared. Flipper One is a Linux computer for everything IP-connected: Wi-Fi, Ethernet, and 5G. It doesn't replace Flipper Zero and doesn't have Flipper Zero's built-in radios.

faq.q: Does Flipper One have a cellular connection out of the box?
faq.a: No. Cellular needs a modem in the M.2 slot, such as our 5G Module. The Nano SIM slot and the built-in eSIM work with the modem you install.

About 90% of the specs are final, and we're still making changes to the hardware. Because of the memory shortage, we can't rule out adjusting some specs, including reducing the amount of RAM. The latest specs are always on the Tech Specs page: https://docs.flipper.net/one/general/tech-specs

Every reward includes one Flipper One. Bundles add the LoRa, SDR, or 5G Module and cost less than buying the same modules as add-ons. Flipper One works without any modules, and you can add them later in our pledge manager.

Kickstarter charges your card when the campaign ends on December 17, not when you back. You can change or cancel your pledge at any time before then. You can also split the payment with Kickstarter's Pledge Over Time.

faq.q: Will Flipper One cost more after Kickstarter?
faq.a: Yes. Kickstarter prices are 25–35% below the estimated retail price.

faq.q: How do I choose the color?
faq.a: Not on Kickstarter. You'll choose the color later, in our pledge manager.
We're aiming to start shipping in July 2027. We'll report on production progress in campaign updates and tell you right away if the date moves.

faq.q: Which countries do you ship to?
faq.a: The United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Australia, all 27 EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Singapore, and Hong Kong. We can't deliver to other countries in this campaign, and we don't ship to freight forwarders or package forwarding services in the US.

faq.q: My country isn't on the list. Can I still get Flipper One?
faq.a: Not in this campaign. We plan to bring Flipper One to more countries after the campaign.

faq.q: Are shipping and taxes included in the price?
faq.a: No. Closer to the shipping date, we'll email you a link to our pledge manager, where you'll confirm your address and pay for shipping and the taxes that apply in your country (sales tax, VAT, or GST). We pay all import duties ourselves, so there's nothing left to pay on delivery.
We estimate shipping at $15–30, depending on your region and what’s in your order. You’ll see the exact cost in our pledge manager before you pay.

faq.q: I don't have a pre-order coupon. Can I still back the campaign?
faq.a: Yes. Coupons are no longer on sale, and you don't need one. Choose any reward on the campaign page.

faq.q: I have a pre-order coupon. How do I use it?
faq.a: Log in to Kickstarter with the email from your pre-order and open the campaign page. You'll see a reward called Flipper One — Pre-order Special. Only coupon holders can see it, and it's reserved for you until December 17. A coupon is not an order: to get your Flipper One, you need to back the campaign with this reward.

faq.q: Does the $20 I paid for the coupon count toward the price?
faq.a: Yes. The price you'll pay on Kickstarter is shown on the Pre-order Special reward.

updates.title: $10M at First Day! Behind The Scenes, Extra Color, Memory (RAM & UFS)
updates.text:
Hi everyone!
We can finally catch our breath and share the first update.
The start of this campaign has been absolutely incredible! With Flipper Zero, it took us a whole month to raise $5 million. With Flipper One, we raised over $10 million on the very first day! And as of right now, we're already the 13th most-funded project in Kickstarter history! WHAT?! 🤯 We never expected anything like this, even in our most optimistic projections.
Thank you all so much for your trust and support. This is a very emotional moment for us because Flipper One is a product we've been dreaming of and working on…
